items.title: Autoregressive Language Model on the 6502 Processor
items.author: nmstoker
items.summary: An autoregressive language model was successfully run on a 6502 processor, demonstrating its capability despite the processor's limited instruction set. The model generated text, showcasing the potential of older hardware for AI tasks. This achievement highlights the efficiency of optimized algorithms on vintage processors.

items.title: RFC 9851: TLS 1.2 is in Feature Freeze
items.author: Jimmc414
items.summary: RFC 9851 confirms TLS 1.2 is in feature freeze, with no further changes except for urgent security updates. TLS 1.3 is recommended due to its improved security. The document was approved in July 2026.

items.title: Show HN: Mu – Tools for Agents
items.author: asim
items.summary: Mu is a tool for AI agents that drafts credible Hacker News comments and posts, respecting community culture by avoiding spam and low-substance content. It prepares thoughtful contributions for users to post at their discretion. The agent emphasizes minimal automation and high-value participation.

items.title: My personal AI benchmark: "Generate an SVG of a frog with a Habsburg jaw."
items.author: thebigship
items.summary: An SVG of a frog with a Habsburg jaw can be generated using AI, referencing the distinctive jawline seen in Habsburg family portraits due to historical inbreeding. This benchmark tests AI's creativity and detail accuracy.

items.title: A tool for finding the causes of unstable Python tests
items.author: pomponchik
items.summary: To find unstable Python tests, use pytest-flakefinder or Trunk Flaky Tests. These tools rerun tests multiple times to identify inconsistencies.

items.title: 'Crush this lady': how eBay harassment campaign led to $56M payout
items.author: JumpCrisscross
items.summary: eBay settled a lawsuit for $56 million after former employees harassed David and Ina Steiner with disturbing packages including insects and pig masks. The harassment followed their critical coverage of the company. The settlement includes compensation and charitable donations.

items.title: Boris Cherny on Trying to Get Claude Code to Rewrite the Claude App
items.author: robenkleene
items.summary: Boris Cherny claims coding is "largely solved" for his work with Claude Code, as he relies entirely on AI for writing code since November 2025. His assertion sparked debate, but he maintains AI handles most programming tasks.

items.title: Connes' Rigidity Theorem: Disproof of Open AI's Counterexample and Proof
items.author: gone35
items.summary: Connes' Rigidity Conjecture was claimed disproved by an OpenAI model, but this was later found invalid. The original claim has not been substantiated, and the conjecture remains unproven. The mathematical community continues to seek a valid proof or disproof.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Ars Notoria and the Promise of Instant Knowledge
items.author: jruohonen
items.summary: Ars Notoria promised instant knowledge and advanced learning shortcuts to medieval scholars. It was criticized for its supposed demonic influence. Anne Lawrence-Mathers studied its history and impact.

items.title: Show HN: MicroCodex Coding Agent – OpenAI/codex reimplemented in C++ <1MB binary
items.author: paoloanzn
items.summary: MicroCodex Coding Agent is a C++ reimplementation of Codex by OpenAI, with a <1MB binary. It aims for efficiency and small size. The project is hosted on GitHub.

items.title: Show HN: Alfa. Killing AI hallucinations with resonance
items.author: SKYNET800
items.text: This code predicts the exact time and price of a future price point, and can also construct a curve of future prices. It can be used to decipher any process that has a graph—for example, a graph of mutual understanding between artificial intelligence and a human.
items.summary: Alfa is a tool designed to combat AI hallucinations by using resonance techniques. It aims to improve AI accuracy and reliability. The project was showcased on Hacker News.

items.title: AI poster wins Ohio State Fair contest
items.author: AlexAplin
items.summary: An AI-generated poster won the Ohio State Fair contest in 2026, sparking controversy. The fair plans to ban AI use in future contests. The winning artist did not break any rules.

items.title: Flock – Chilling Effects: Long Island's Emerging Open-Air Prison
items.author: mediaeater
items.summary: Long Island's emerging open-air prison concept involves incarcerated individuals managing a turkey flock. This initiative aims to provide rehabilitation and work opportunities. The idea is inspired by historical prison practices.

items.title: Let kids be kids: When collectibles lose their playfulness
items.author: capitain
items.summary: Toys that no longer encourage imaginative play can hinder children's development. Letting kids play independently fosters creativity and problem-solving skills. It's often best to let children create their own memories instead of keeping old memorabilia.
